name: Factory
summary: A software factory on your kehikko: builds judged by a panel of agents, and /review-factory for accurate, transparent reviews of pull and merge requests.
guidance: Factory runs features through a pipeline of agents (spec, plan, build, review, counter-argument, judge) when the person types /factory in a Claude Code conversation. Its MCP door only reads: `jobs` lists a project's jobs and their stages, `job` reads one job's files (spec, plan, reviews, counter-arguments, judgements, decision). You cannot start, approve, merge or send back a job: those are the person's, typed or pressed. Never merge a factory/<job> branch yourself. It also runs /review-factory, a review panel for pull and merge requests (planner, two reviewers, an adversary, a judge) that drafts into Review: `reviews` lists a project's reviews, `review` reads one and its record ("How this review was made"). You cannot start, steer or send a review.

mcp.about: The jobs of the software factory in a project, and each job's files; the /review-factory reviews and their records. Read-only.

settings.label: Let the judge merge approved jobs by itself
settings.description: An approved job is merged into main without waiting for you. Off: approved jobs wait for you.

settings.label: Post two-way reviews by myself
settings.description: A two-way change with no UI or UX is posted to the pull or merge request without you, through Review.

settings.label: Re-review by myself
settings.description: When a change is ready for another review, it runs in a background session without asking you.

settings.label: Reviewers may run this project's tests
settings.description: Only the project's own test command, in the review's checkout.

settings.label: Ready for another review
settings.description: The signal that an author is ready for another review, unless you set one for them.
settings.default: when they re-request review, or 2 hours after the last push with new commits and every point answered

settings.label: Door rules
settings.description: One rule a line: "path migrations/ → one-way" or "label two-way → two-way". A one-way rule always wins.
